lessons.title: Use CTEs
lessons.summary: Break complex queries into named steps.
lessons.explanation: WITH creates temporary named result sets that can be referenced by the final SELECT.
lessons.example:
WITH revenue_by_order AS (
  SELECT order_id, SUM(quantity * unit_price) AS revenue
  FROM sales
  GROUP BY order_id
)
SELECT o.id, c.name, r.revenue
FROM revenue_by_order r
JOIN orders o ON o.id = r.order_id
JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id;

exercises.prompt: Find paid orders with revenue over 1000. Return columns: id, name, revenue. Order by: o.id ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: WITH revenue_by_order AS (SELECT order_id, SUM(quantity * unit_price) AS revenue FROM sales GROUP BY order_id) SELECT o.id, c.name, r.revenue FROM revenue_by_order r JOIN orders o ON o.id = r.order_id JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'paid' AND r.revenue > 1000 ORDER BY o.id;

exercises.prompt: Use a CTE to find departments with an average salary above 85000. Return columns: name, average_salary. Order by: name ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: WITH department_salary AS (SELECT d.name, AVG(e.salary) AS average_salary FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON d.id = e.department_id GROUP BY d.name) SELECT name, average_salary FROM department_salary WHERE average_salary > 85000 ORDER BY name;

exercises.prompt: Use a CTE to calculate project workload and show projects over 40 hours per week. Return columns: name, total_hours. Order by: name ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: WITH project_hours AS (SELECT p.name, SUM(ep.hours_per_week) AS total_hours FROM employee_projects ep JOIN projects p ON p.id = ep.project_id GROUP BY p.name) SELECT name, total_hours FROM project_hours WHERE total_hours > 40 ORDER BY name;

exercises.prompt: Use a CTE to show each customer's total paid revenue. Return columns: name, revenue. Order by: c.name ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: WITH paid_revenue AS (SELECT o.customer_id, SUM(s.quantity * s.unit_price) AS revenue FROM orders o JOIN sales s ON s.order_id = o.id WHERE o.status = 'paid' GROUP BY o.customer_id) SELECT c.name, p.revenue FROM paid_revenue p JOIN customers c ON c.id = p.customer_id ORDER BY c.name;

exercises.prompt: Use a CTE to find employees assigned to more than one project. Return columns: first_name, last_name, project_count. Order by: e.id ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: WITH assignment_counts AS (SELECT employee_id, COUNT(*) AS project_count FROM employee_projects GROUP BY employee_id) SELECT e.first_name, e.last_name, a.project_count FROM assignment_counts a JOIN employees e ON e.id = a.employee_id WHERE a.project_count > 1 ORDER BY e.id;

lessons.title: Use Subqueries
lessons.explanation: A subquery can calculate a value or list of values that the outer query uses for filtering.

exercises.prompt: Find employees whose salary is above the company average. Return columns: first_name, last_name, salary. Order by: id ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT first_name, last_name, salary FROM employees WHERE salary > (SELECT AVG(salary) FROM employees) ORDER BY id;

exercises.prompt: Find projects with a budget above the average project budget. Return columns: name, budget. Order by: id ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT name, budget FROM projects WHERE budget > (SELECT AVG(budget) FROM projects) ORDER BY id;

exercises.prompt: Find customers who have placed at least one paid order. Return columns: name, city. Order by: id ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT name, city FROM customers WHERE id IN (SELECT customer_id FROM orders WHERE status = 'paid') ORDER BY id;

exercises.prompt: Find products whose unit price is above the average unit price. Return columns: product, unit_price. Order by: id ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT product, unit_price FROM sales WHERE unit_price > (SELECT AVG(unit_price) FROM sales) ORDER BY id;

exercises.prompt: Find employees who are assigned to any project. Return columns: first_name, last_name. Order by: id ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT first_name, last_name FROM employees WHERE id IN (SELECT employee_id FROM employee_projects) ORDER BY id;

lessons.title: Window Functions
lessons.summary: Calculate values across related rows without collapsing them.
lessons.explanation: Window functions use OVER to calculate rankings, totals, and comparisons while keeping row-level detail.

exercises.prompt: Rank employees by salary from highest to lowest. Return columns: first_name, last_name, salary, salary_rank. Order by: salary_rank ASC, id ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT first_name, last_name, salary, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC) AS salary_rank FROM employees ORDER BY salary_rank, id;

exercises.prompt: Show each employee with the average salary of their department. Return columns: first_name, last_name, department_id, salary, department_average. Order by: id ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT first_name, last_name, department_id, salary, AVG(salary) OVER (PARTITION BY department_id) AS department_average FROM employees ORDER BY id;

exercises.prompt: Number orders from oldest to newest. Return columns: id, order_date, status, order_number. Order by: order_number ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT id, order_date, status, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY order_date ASC) AS order_number FROM orders ORDER BY order_number;

exercises.prompt: Show each sale with total revenue for its category. Return columns: product, category, line_revenue, category_revenue. Order by: id ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT product, category, quantity * unit_price AS line_revenue, SUM(quantity * unit_price) OVER (PARTITION BY category) AS category_revenue FROM sales ORDER BY id;

exercises.prompt: Rank projects by budget from largest to smallest. Return columns: name, budget, budget_rank. Order by: budget_rank ASC, id ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT name, budget, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY budget DESC) AS budget_rank FROM projects ORDER BY budget_rank, id;

lessons.title: Use LAG
lessons.summary: Compare each row with a previous row.
lessons.explanation: LAG(column) looks back to a previous row in the same window. Use OVER (ORDER BY ...) to define the row order, and PARTITION BY to compare previous values inside each group.

exercises.prompt: Show orders with the previous order date. Return columns: id, order_date, previous_order_date. Order by: order_date ASC, id ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT id, order_date, LAG(order_date) OVER (ORDER BY order_date, id) AS previous_order_date FROM orders ORDER BY order_date, id;

exercises.prompt: Show employees with the previous employee hire date. Return columns: first_name, last_name, hire_date, previous_hire_date. Order by: hire_date ASC, id ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT first_name, last_name, hire_date, LAG(hire_date) OVER (ORDER BY hire_date, id) AS previous_hire_date FROM employees ORDER BY hire_date, id;

exercises.prompt: Show projects with the previous larger project budget. Return columns: name, budget, previous_budget. Order by: budget DESC, id ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT name, budget, LAG(budget) OVER (ORDER BY budget DESC, id) AS previous_budget FROM projects ORDER BY budget DESC, id;

exercises.prompt: Show sales rows with the previous line revenue inside each category. Return columns: product, category, line_revenue, previous_category_revenue. Order by: category ASC, line_revenue DESC, id ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT product, category, quantity * unit_price AS line_revenue, LAG(quantity * unit_price) OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY quantity * unit_price DESC, id) AS previous_category_revenue FROM sales ORDER BY category, line_revenue DESC, id;

exercises.prompt: Show order revenue and the change from the previous order's revenue. Return columns: id, order_date, revenue, revenue_change. Order by: order_date ASC, id ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: WITH order_revenue AS (SELECT o.id, o.order_date, SUM(s.quantity * s.unit_price) AS revenue FROM orders o JOIN sales s ON s.order_id = o.id GROUP BY o.id, o.order_date) SELECT id, order_date, revenue, revenue - LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY order_date, id) AS revenue_change FROM order_revenue ORDER BY order_date, id;

exercises.prompt: Show employees with the previous salary inside their department. Return columns: first_name, last_name, department_id, salary, previous_department_salary. Order by: department_id ASC, salary DESC, id ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT first_name, last_name, department_id, salary, LAG(salary) OVER (PARTITION BY department_id ORDER BY salary DESC, id) AS previous_department_salary FROM employees ORDER BY department_id, salary DESC, id;

exercises.prompt: Show project assignments with the previous assignment date inside each project. Return columns: project_id, employee_id, assigned_on, previous_project_assigned_on. Order by: project_id ASC, assigned_on ASC, employee_id ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT project_id, employee_id, assigned_on, LAG(assigned_on) OVER (PARTITION BY project_id ORDER BY assigned_on, employee_id) AS previous_project_assigned_on FROM employee_projects ORDER BY project_id, assigned_on, employee_id;

exercises.prompt: Show customers with the previous customer name inside each segment. Return columns: name, segment, previous_segment_customer. Order by: segment ASC, name ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT name, segment, LAG(name) OVER (PARTITION BY segment ORDER BY name) AS previous_segment_customer FROM customers ORDER BY segment, name;

exercises.prompt: Show sales with the previous unit price for the same product. Return columns: product, order_date, unit_price, previous_product_unit_price. Order by: product ASC, order_date ASC, id ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT s.product, o.order_date, s.unit_price, LAG(s.unit_price) OVER (PARTITION BY s.product ORDER BY o.order_date, s.id) AS previous_product_unit_price FROM sales s JOIN orders o ON o.id = s.order_id ORDER BY s.product, o.order_date, s.id;

exercises.prompt: Show each customer's orders with their previous order status. Return columns: customer_id, id, order_date, status, previous_customer_status. Order by: customer_id ASC, order_date ASC, id ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT customer_id, id, order_date, status, LAG(status) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date, id) AS previous_customer_status FROM orders ORDER BY customer_id, order_date, id;

exercises.prompt: Show employees with the previous hired employee's salary. Return columns: first_name, last_name, hire_date, salary, previous_hire_salary. Order by: hire_date ASC, id ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT first_name, last_name, hire_date, salary, LAG(salary) OVER (ORDER BY hire_date, id) AS previous_hire_salary FROM employees ORDER BY hire_date, id;

exercises.prompt: Show project workload totals with the previous workload total. Return columns: name, total_hours, previous_total_hours. Order by: total_hours DESC, name ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: WITH project_hours AS (SELECT p.name, SUM(ep.hours_per_week) AS total_hours FROM projects p JOIN employee_projects ep ON ep.project_id = p.id GROUP BY p.name) SELECT name, total_hours, LAG(total_hours) OVER (ORDER BY total_hours DESC, name) AS previous_total_hours FROM project_hours ORDER BY total_hours DESC, name;

exercises.prompt: Show paid orders with the previous paid order date. Return columns: id, order_date, previous_paid_order_date. Order by: order_date ASC, id ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT id, order_date, LAG(order_date) OVER (ORDER BY order_date, id) AS previous_paid_order_date FROM orders WHERE status = 'paid' ORDER BY order_date, id;

exercises.prompt: Show sales line items with the previous line revenue by sale id. Return columns: id, product, line_revenue, previous_line_revenue. Order by: id ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: SELECT id, product, quantity * unit_price AS line_revenue, LAG(quantity * unit_price) OVER (ORDER BY id) AS previous_line_revenue FROM sales ORDER BY id;

exercises.prompt: Show customer order revenue with the previous revenue for the same customer. Return columns: customer_id, id, order_date, revenue, previous_customer_revenue. Order by: customer_id ASC, order_date ASC, id ASC.
exercises.expectedSql: WITH order_revenue AS (SELECT o.customer_id, o.id, o.order_date, SUM(s.quantity * s.unit_price) AS revenue FROM orders o JOIN sales s ON s.order_id = o.id GROUP BY o.customer_id, o.id, o.order_date) SELECT customer_id, id, order_date, revenue, LAG(revenue) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY order_date, id) AS previous_customer_revenue FROM order_revenue ORDER BY customer_id, order_date, id;
